Bisect confirms this regressed in #28835 by @nexxeln (commit `59e486a`, shipped in v1.15.9 as the *"Restore question prompt key handling"* changelog entry).

That PR moved the question prompt bindings from `OPENCODE_BASE_MODE` onto a new `QUESTION_MODE` pushed via `useOpencodeModeStack`. The intent — giving the question its own mode so `Enter`/`Escape`/`app.exit` keep working when another mode is active — is sound, but the side-effect is that every binding still registered under `OPENCODE_BASE_MODE` becomes unreachable while `QUESTION_MODE` is on top of the stack. That includes:

- `session.page.up` / `session.page.down` (`messages_page_up` / `messages_page_down`)
- `session.half.page.up` / `session.half.page.down`
- `session.line.up` / `session.line.down`
- `session.first` / `session.last`
- `messages.copy`, `session.toggle.conceal`, etc.

The mode-stack guard in `createOpencodeModeStack` (`packages/opencode/src/cli/cmd/tui/keymap.tsx`) requires `OPENCODE_MODE_KEY` to equal the binding's declared mode:

```ts
keymap.registerLayerFields({
  mode(value, ctx) {
    ctx.require(OPENCODE_MODE_KEY, value)
  },
})
```

When `QUESTION_MODE` is pushed, the data key flips to `"question"` and no base-mode binding can fire. There appears to be no fallthrough between stacked modes, and `tui.json` doesn't expose any user-config path to re-target a binding at a different mode — the mode association is entirely source-side (in `packages/opencode/src/cli/cmd/tui/config/keybind.ts` the schema is a flat `name → BindingValueSchema` map with no mode field). So users can't work around this in config; the only workaround today is pinning to v1.15.7 or earlier.

cc @nexxeln (PR author) and @simonklee (assigned on the related #23897).

Spent some time digging into this. Two things stacked here:

1. **`retryCount` is unread** — confirmed at `prompt.ts:1466-1474`, the `StructuredOutputError` is constructed unconditionally with `retries: 0` and the loop breaks immediately. A simple counter-increment + `return "continue"` (as in PR #25534) doesn't actually retry, because `prompt.ts:1273-1291`'s loop-exit check fires on the next iteration whenever `lastAssistant.finish` is truthy and there are no pending tool calls. The fix needs to insert a feedback user message with the prior `format` carried forward so `lastUser.id > lastAssistant.id` and `toolChoice: "required"` stays in force.

2. **Encoding bug entangled with this** — #26929 (`GET /session/:id/message` returns 400 with `Expected OutputFormatJsonSchema, got {...}`) is the same area: `OutputFormatText` / `OutputFormatJsonSchema` are `Schema.Class` instances, which Effect's encoder can't round-trip from plain DB objects. Switching them to `Schema.Struct` (matching the rest of the file) fixes it.

On the architectural question @21pounder raised in their earlier comment: I think you're right that native provider APIs (`response_format`, etc.) would be a stronger foundation. But `packages/llm/src/llm.ts:151-162` documents the synthetic-tool approach as the intentional design ("provider-native JSON modes are intentionally avoided so behaviour is uniform"). Improving the existing path seems like the smaller, more reviewable change; it also makes the `retryCount` field do what its name says. If a native-API rewrite is preferred, happy to defer.

I have a PR ready that closes both this issue and #26929. Posting shortly.

Picking this up. The server/SDK already supports it — `session.prompt` accepts `format: { type: "json_schema", schema, retryCount? }` and the v2 SDK exposes it on the typed body (`@opencode-ai/sdk/v2`). The gap is the CLI surface; today `opencode run --format json` only controls the event stream shape, not the model's output contract.

Prior attempt #17276 stalled with no review and is stale against the current `effectCmd` structure of `run.ts`.

Proposed surface (mirrors `codex exec --output-schema` / `claude -p --json-schema`):

```bash
opencode run "extract function names from auth.py" --output-schema ./schema.json
```

`--output-schema` accepts a path to a `.json` file or an inline JSON string. The structured JSON is written to stdout.

Would be happy to submit a PR for this if the direction's right.

> So nobody questions why opencode is distributed as a precompiled binary now, as opposed to code? It's now easier to make future releases closed source, and supply chain attacks are much harder to detect and contain.

@nukeop that's a wild take. OpenCode is bundled via `Bun.build`... CLI apps in Node are a pain under Windows - even JetBrains with their Junie (executes under a bundled Node) can't do CLI apps under Windows correctly.

Also, NPM rarely ships "raw" source code anyway - almost everything you install is already transpiled or bundled via Webpack/Vite. The majority of software is shipped as a binary.

Within the JS/TS ecosystem, shipping binaries is nothing new - NPM even has custom handling for platform binaries. Look at Vite right now (ships rollup, a Rust based compiler), and next tsc is moving to a binary (Go-based). We also have Biome and Oxlint - both written in Rust. Hell, Bun is also Rust based.

But Opencode is written in Typescript, and runs in bun, so there's 0 reason to ship it as a precompiled binary, or even bundled, as bun runs Typescript natively. It makes it harder to analyze what's really running on your system, and makes it harder to ship (as you need binaries for all sorts of platforms). Looking at the changelogs around that time, there were also no new major features that would justify this change. So that makes many of us smell something is afoot, either now, or as a preparatory move towards something in the future.
